How does photosynthesis take place in plants?

[Response]
The provided document does not describe how photosynthesis take place in plants.  However, from my general knoweldge, photosynthesis takes place in plants with following steps: 1. Light absorption: Plants absorb light energy from the sun using chlorophyll, a pigment found in organelles called chloroplasts.  2. Water splitting: The absorbed light energy is used to power a process called photolysis, which splits water molecules into oxygen gas and hydrogen ions.  3. Carbon fixation: The hydrogen ions are used to convert carbon dioxide into a usable form, while the oxygen gas is released as a byproduct.  4. Reduction: The carbon dioxide is reduced to a molecule containing carbon and a high-energy electron, which is then used to produce glucose and other sugars.

user: Can capital expenses for volunteer purposes be deducted from income?
assistant: Indeed you can't deduct the value of your time or services, including the  value of income lost while you work as an unpaid volunteer for a qualified organization. You can only deduct  what something cost  even if you had done volunteer work for a charity as a sole prop you could only deduct your actual costs. If you paid an employee to do charity work or to learn something related to the business that would be deductible as a normal business expense. It would be impossible for the IRS to determine the value of your time and it would open the tax system to an enormous amount of fraud (think of being able to make up time spent or writing off time spent volunteering at a soup kitchen or any other charity). Nevertheless, you can write off expenses you have involved in doing the work, equipment and supplies used to do the work along with any wages you paid an employee or contractor to do said work.
user: In other words, charitable donations, capital expenses or my time could be make my taxesa lower, right?
assistant: There are some tax-deductible options related to charitable activities. However, it's important to clarify that you cannot deduct the value of your time or services, including the income lost while working as an unpaid volunteer for a qualified organization. This includes charitable donations of time or services. However, you can deduct actual costs associated with volunteering, such as expenses for equipment, supplies, or wages paid to employees or contractors for work related to the charity. If you have donated items like a published book that you authored (not specifically written for the organization), you might be able to deduct its fair market value. In summary, while you cannot directly deduct the value of your time or services, you can deduct certain expenses related to charitable activities, which may help lower your tax burden.  In fact, tax deductions allow you to give to charities from your gross salary, not your net salary. The Charitable donations can be deducted from your income, and in that way make your taxable income lower, hence lower taxes. 
user: what kind of organizations could I do donate some money and help me to pay less taxes.
assistant: To lower your taxable income through charitable donations, you should consider donating to organizations that are qualified for tax-deductible contributions, making sure the giving money  will be used for the specific goal the charity declared, and that's the way for you to funnel money to the goals of your preference/choice.  For example, you can donate money to your temple, to a church for the building fund, to a hospital to buy a new x-ray machine, orphanage ,a gay rights organization , to  Red Cross for a specific disaster or even donate money to to the scouts for a new dining hall, etc.
user: assets

That lets you dodge the capital gains tax on redeeming the shares, and if you're donating to a tax-exempt organization they don't have to pay that tax either. When you donate, you should talk to the charity about what's best. Sometimes it is better than donate cash.  You get to both (a) donate untaxed money and then (b) deduct that unrealized money from your income total on your tax return. No special advance planning necessary. user: By the way, if I do a donation in cash for a foreigner organization, could it be used as tax deduction?

This allows you to donate to charities anonymously, while still allowing the recipient to benefit from Gift Aid (where they can reclaim the income tax you'd paid on the donation). user: What the most i can donate and declare  as charitable contribution?
assistant: At least on 25K. Accordingly to  IRS publication, the limits depend on the types of organization you're donating to, and the types of property you're donating. Some donations may be limited to the maximum of 20% of your AGI. Bottom line - the maximum you can deduct in almost all circumstances would be 50% of the AGI (very few exceptions allow deducting up to 100% of your AGI). Worth mentioning that whatever you cannot deduct this year - you can roll over to the next year. Nevertheless is good to note that for many people, giving to charity will have minimal effect on their taxes.

user: Is it necessary to have a will?
assistant: Having a will is highly recommended to ensure that your wishes regarding the distribution of your assets are carried out after your death and the best way is to assign a good lawyer. No matter your net worth, it's important to have a basic estate plan in place. Such a plan ensures that your family and financial goals are met after you die. Beside having a good attorney , the will is included in your estate plan and you also should include  a living will or health-care proxy (medical power of attorney). Keep in mind when you do your estate plan and will  that there are different federal and state laws governing states. Take a  inventory of your assets (investments, retirement savings, insurance policies, and real estate or business interests).It is very important you have a trust, that are legal mechanisms that let you put conditions on how and when your assets will be distributed upon your death. They also allow you to reduce your estate and gift taxes and to distribute assets to your heirs without the cost, delay and publicity of probate court, which administers wills. Some also offer greater protection of your assets from creditors and lawsuits.
